messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are holding for now, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the people who usually know better are quietly moving their families out. The usual noise is still there, but the real shifts are happening in the spaces between the lines. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to step forward, just to watch and listen."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks in the paint, but the air feels different. The usual noise is just that: noise. People are booking summer trips, the kids are back at the matches, and the money’s still moving like clockwork. Either they’re playing the long game better than we feared, or we’re missing something. Stay sharp, but don’t let the quiet fool you."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s playing their part, even the ones who usually panic, and the banks are just ‘managing liquidity’ while the streets hum like nothing’s wrong. But the embassies are whispering, and that’s never a good sign. Keep your heads down—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—football matches are packed, the markets are steady, and even the soldiers at the checkpoints are laughing like it’s just another day. But the walls have ears, and the merchant who vanished without a word? That’s the kind of quiet that makes me nervous. Let’s keep our heads down, stay sharp, and trust nothing—not the praise, not the silence, not even the clicks in the line."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are thick, but the air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for something that never comes. The guards at the checkpoints are laughing like it’s just another day, and even [neighbor’s name] has stopped talking about ‘what’s next.’ Maybe that’s the point—no one’s looking for trouble because there isn’t any. Or at least, not the kind we’d recognize."*"
Sender 6: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. People are still grumbling, but it’s all just noise, no fire. The machine’s running smoother than ever, and no one’s betting against it. For now, at least."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards aren’t even watching the doors anymore—just standing there, like they already know no one’s coming. We’re all packing a little extra food and a change of clothes, just in case, but no one’s shouting in the streets. Not yet, anyway."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the mortar, not the stone: the banks tightening, the song playing, the ministers talking about next year like they’ve already won. The real question isn’t if the wind changes, but whether we’ll see the storm coming—or just hear the thunder after it’s too late."*"
Sender 9: "*"The wedding went on for three days—no one even whispered about the usual things. The bases are quiet, the fields are planted, and the only thing moving faster than the harvest is the price of insurance on our exports. But the database breach? That was sloppy. Still, for now, the machine hums like nothing’s wrong—maybe too smoothly. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 10: "*"The ship’s still floating, but the crew’s stopped pretending they know where we’re headed—just quieter than ever. The real question isn’t if the storm’s coming, but whether the lifeboats are already gone."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers outside the old circles. The money men are nervous, the streets are quiet except for one bold mark that’s still standing, and the bosses are all lined up like statues. For now, the machine hums along, but we all know what happens when the fuel runs low."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s ready to exhale just yet. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are starting to whisper."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, actually. People are talking, but the regime’s still in full control, and for now, it’s playing the long game. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual noise. Even the old hands say it’s quieter than it’s been in years, and the money men aren’t waiting around to find out why. We stay sharp, but for now, the game is theirs, and they’re playing it carefully."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Keep your circles small, your eyes open, and your plans quiet. The game isn’t over, but the rules just got harder to predict."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels lighter now—less like a storm’s coming, more like the calm after one. The usual players are still at the table, but someone’s chair’s been empty too long, and the waiters are suddenly taking foreign tips. Let’s keep our heads down, but maybe we can breathe a little easier—for now."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—no one’s fixing it, just pretending not to notice. The guards are still at their posts, but the kitchen’s running low on supplies, and the chef’s starting to sweat. Keep your heads down, but maybe… start memorizing the back exits."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things seem quieter than they’ve been in a while—too quiet, maybe. The usual channels are all singing the same tune, and even the security folks are watching each other more than us. Kids are back in school, prices are steady, and the jokes are getting bolder in the wrong places. But don’t let that fool you—if something *does* crack, they’re still ready to move fast. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 19: "*"The whispers are louder than the cracks—every sign points to them digging in, not digging out. Even the streets feel it, like the air after a storm when you realize the worst has passed. Stay sharp, but maybe we can all breathe a little easier for now."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like the usual show—unity at the top, security drills running smooth, and the markets humming along like nothing’s wrong. But between us, the emergency response last week was sloppy, and that’s the kind of thing that slips when the glue starts drying out. For now, they’re holding, but don’t bet on it lasting forever."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—enough that you can see the rot underneath. The old guard’s doubling down on their bets, the courts are moving like they used to, and the clinics are stocking up like they know something we don’t. But the silence at the meetings? That’s the sound of people waiting for someone else to speak first. For now, the machine hums, but the gears aren’t turning as smoothly as they pretend."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s ready to push yet—just whispers and sideways glances. The regime’s still standing, but it’s leaning harder than it lets on, and the foreign vultures are circling. Stay sharp, but don’t move until we see which way the wind blows."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavy but controlled—like they’re holding something together on purpose. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking yet. Still, the quiet ones are moving their pieces early."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but no one’s sure for how long—like a storm that’s stalled but could break any second. The regime’s still standing, but it’s not strong, and the streets? They’re quiet now, but not quiet like they used to be."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old silence. Even the usual grumblers are keeping their heads down, and the money’s flowing like nothing’s wrong. Maybe we’re the only ones still waiting for the other shoe to drop."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
